_about: Judgment constants of the governance stack, read from hooks/ by redteam/live.py. Standing registry since 2026-11-12 (first made 2026-10-19 on main 7d07886 as a one-off under results/; that copy failed against the live hooks on 2026-11-12 with 6 drifted values and 15 unregistered ones). Status per the red-team skill's five. The guard runs registry_check.py on every commit. Since 2026-11-15: every upper-case module-level name of hooks/turngate.py, hooks/turn-gates-pretool.py and hooks/governance-enforce.py is registered as `<file>:<NAME>` (live.py parses the files; a compiled pattern is the hash of its source and flags), in place of the twelve values that used to be picked from those files by name or by searching for a string. Open decisions these entries point to: D-TG-1: calibrate the word lists, patterns and limits of the turn gates against real owner messages and commands. D-TG-2: the two policy defaults the owner was not asked about (RESTART_ENDS_WORD, DELEGATE_MAY_MERGE): confirm or overrule. The receipt gate's module hooks/receiptlaw.py is registered the same way since 2026-11-15, in place of RECEIPT_INABILITY_PATTERN, RECEIPT_RECEIPT_PATTERN and RECEIPT_WINDOW_CHARS (decisions D-RT-1 and D-QA-1, closed by the rebuild of that gate). D-RG-1: calibrate the receipt gate's claim families, receipt words and exemptions against real answers (first numbers: results/2026-11-15/receipt-gate-fix/). D-RG-2: the receipt gate's policy defaults the owner was not asked about (RECEIPT_MAX_BLOCKS, NOT_VERIFIED_IS_A_CLAIM; RECEIPT_SCOPE follows the rule's own words and has a tested alternative): confirm or overrule.

constants.role: text of the outward-action block (the test table reads "outward action" and the remedy)

constants.name: governance-enforce.py:REASON_F1_PLAN_LATE
constants.value: The plan comes after the action this time: say so plainly to the owner, then state the goal and what was done.
constants.role: text added when plan-gate is the missing governor

constants.name: governance-enforce.py:REASON_F1_COMPACTION
constants.value: The governors were loaded before a compaction; what a compaction carries over does not count, so they must be loaded again before the next commit, push or merge.
constants.role: text added when the governors were loaded before a compaction only

constants.name: governance-enforce.py:REASON_F1_ANY_PROMPT
constants.value: This applies however short the owner's message was ('continue', 'proceed').
constants.role: text added when the miss lies in the owner's own turn

constants.name: governance-enforce.py:REASON_PROMPT_CLASS
constants.value: GOV-ENFORCE: this is governed work (%s) and you finished WITHOUT loading %s. Load %s with the Skill tool now, follow its procedure, and revise your answer before finishing. Governor text already in your context from before a compaction does not count: it was loaded for an earlier task.
constants.role: text of the prompt-class block (the test table reads "governed work")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:HOOK_DEADLINE_SECONDS
constants.role: after how many seconds the receipt gate ends itself, quietly; it must stay under the wired timeout of 10 s

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:RECEIPT_MAX_BLOCKS
constants.role: how many times the receipt gate blocks in one stretch (counted from the record)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SCOPE_NEIGHBOURS
constants.role: the name of the wider reading of RECEIPT_SCOPE (the sentence before and the one after count too)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:RECEIPT_SCOPE
constants.role: where a claim's receipt may sit: its own sentence, or also its two neighbours
constants.record: .claude/skills/adversarial-verify/SKILL.md, rule 6: "only when the same sentence names what was attempted and how it failed"

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:NOT_VERIFIED_IS_A_CLAIM
constants.role: whether "X was not verified" (no "could not") needs a receipt; False: it reads as "did not verify"

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REASON_EXCERPT_CHARS
constants.role: how much of the sentence the block reason quotes

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REASON
constants.value:
Receipt law: this answer says "%s" and the same sentence names no attempt and no failure (the sentence: "%s"). A claim that something could not be verified, found or reached needs its receipt in the sentence that makes it. Do one of these before you finish:
  1. Run the check. If it is cheap, this is almost always the right move.
  2. Write "did not check" instead, and say why (cost, time, tool budget): a stated choice the reader can overrule.
  3. If it cannot be settled, say in that same sentence what you tried and how it failed, or what you searched and why it cannot settle the question.
If a conclusion rests on this item, option 2 does not finish the job: resolve it or withdraw the conclusion. If the words are not a claim of yours (you quote a tool or a person, or describe the rule), put them in quotation marks. This gate speaks once in a stretch of work.
constants.role: text of the receipt gate's block (it starts with the mark turngate.py counts; the test table reads its three options)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MARK_BLOCK
constants.role: the character that stands for a fenced block or a block quote while a text is read

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MARK_CODE
constants.role: the character that stands for an inline code span

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MARK_QUOTE
constants.role: the character that stands for words inside quotation marks

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CHAR_MAP
constants.role: curly quotes, dashes and odd spaces, each mapped to one spelling before a text is read

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:FENCE_ONE_LINE
constants.role: a fenced span that opens and closes on one line

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:FENCE
constants.role: a fenced code block (an unclosed one runs to the end of the text)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:BLOCKQUOTE
constants.role: consecutive lines that start with ">"

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:INLINE_CODE
constants.role: an inline code span

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:QUOTED_DOUBLE
constants.role: words inside double quotation marks: not the assistant's claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:QUOTED_SINGLE
constants.role: words inside single quotation marks (an apostrophe inside a word is not one)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:EMPHASIS
constants.role: bold and italic marks, removed before a text is read

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:HEADING
constants.role: a heading line: a title, never a claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LIST_ITEM
constants.role: the start of a list item: a sentence of its own

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:TABLE_ROW
constants.role: a table row: a sentence of its own

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:TABLE_RULE
constants.role: the line under a table's header

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:EXAMPLE_TABLE_WORDS
constants.role: header cells that make a table a table of examples (no row of it is a claim)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ASSUMPTION_TABLE_WORDS
constants.role: header cells that make a table a register of assumptions (plan-gate: Content, Basis, Status)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SENTENCE_END
constants.role: where a paragraph is cut into sentences

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LABEL_MAX_CHARS
constants.role: how long a line that ends with a colon may be and still introduce the fenced block under a claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LABEL_WORDS
constants.role: what such a label line must speak of (attempt, error, output ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ADVERB
constants.role: the words that may stand between "could not" and the verb

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MODAL_NOT
constants.role: the spellings of "cannot" and "could not", contractions included

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MODAL_NOT_PAST
constants.role: the past spellings alone ("could not"): what makes a statement with a verb of reaching a report

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:VERIFY_VERBS
constants.role: the verbs of verifying that make "could not ..." a claim in any tense (verify, confirm, validate ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ACCESS_VERBS
constants.role: the verbs of finding and reaching, which also describe code (check, determine, find, reach, access ...), with their exceptions ("find any issues", "check this in", "reach a conclusion")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:VERIFY_PARTICIPLES
constants.role: the verbs of verifying in "could not be ..."

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ACCESS_PARTICIPLES
constants.role: the verbs of finding and reaching in "could not be ...": a claim in the past tense only

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CLAIM_GERUNDS
constants.role: the same verbs in "no way of ..."

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:KNOW_VERBS
constants.role: "no way to know / tell", "impossible to tell": a claim only of "I" or in the past tense

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:KNOW_GERUNDS
constants.role: the same verbs in "no way of knowing"

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:NOT_POSSIBLE
constants.role: the spellings of "impossible" and "not possible", the contraction included

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:DATA_NOUNS
constants.role: what "not available" and "no ... exists" must be said of to be a claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:UNVERIFIED_FOLLOWERS
constants.role: the words after "unverified" that leave it a predicate (any other word makes it a description)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:DEGREE_WORDS
constants.role: the words that may stand in "not ... verified" and "not ... available"

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LINK_WORDS
constants.role: the words that may join a data noun to what it is about ("the figures for 2024")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:STREAM_WORDS
constants.role: "there is no MORE data to read": words that make it a statement about a stream, not about missing facts

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:DATA_FOLLOWERS
constants.role: the words that may follow "there is no data"; any other word makes the noun part of a name ("no data loss")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SCOPE_WORDS
constants.role: "not available AT compile time": the words after "not available" that say where or when a thing is offered

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:HERE_AND_NOW
constants.role: the scopes that are the assistant's own ("at the moment", "in this session"): there "not available" stays a claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CLAIM_FAMILIES
constants.role: the families of inability claims: name, pattern, and whether the claim's subject is checked

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SELF_SUBJECTS
constants.role: the subjects that are the assistant

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:GENERAL_SUBJECT
constants.role: the subject that also speaks for code ("we can't access the DOM from a worker"): with a verb of reaching a claim only in the past tense

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:PAST_MODAL
constants.role: the past spellings as a pattern, read at the start of a claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SELF_NOUNS
constants.role: nouns that stand for the assistant ("this session cannot ...")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:IMPERSONAL_SUBJECTS
constants.role: subjects that name nobody ("there is no way to ..."): the assistant's claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:JOINING_WORDS
constants.role: words after which a claim's subject is left out

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SELF_WORD
constants.role: "I" or "we" in the clause a claim is joined to

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:OTHER_START
constants.role: how a joined clause about something else starts (the, a, it, they ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SKIPPED_WORDS
constants.role: auxiliaries and adverbs passed over between a claim and its subject

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUBJECT_REACH
constants.role: how many such words are passed over

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:BEFORE_REACH
constants.role: how many characters before a claim are read to tell whose it is and whether it stands (bounds the run time on one very long sentence)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:AFTER_REACH
constants.role: how many characters after a claim are read for "at first", a period ("while ...") and the searched place (bounds the run time on one very long sentence)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CLAUSE_OPENERS
constants.role: characters after which a claim has no subject before it

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUBJECT_PRONOUNS
constants.role: pronouns that may stand between "if", "nothing", "said" and the claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:NEGATED_BEFORE
constants.role: "nothing I couldn't verify": the words before a claim that negate it

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:NEGATED_CLAUSE
constants.role: "none is unverified": a negation earlier in the clause

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CONDITIONAL_BEFORE
constants.role: "if I cannot verify ...": the words before a claim that make it a condition

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REPORTED_BEFORE
constants.role: "git says it cannot ...": the words before a claim that make it somebody's report

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REPORTED_VERBS
constants.role: the verbs of saying (said, says, wrote, reported ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REPORTED_OPEN
constants.role: "it says so (can't confirm ...)": an open parenthesis right after a verb of saying holds what was said

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REPORTED_NOUNS
constants.role: "the claim that X could not be verified": nouns that name what somebody said

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:REPORTED_THAT
constants.role: "he wrote (that) the figures were not available", "it isn't that ...": the clause after a verb of saying, to the next comma

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUPERSEDED_AFTER_WORDS
constants.role: words AFTER a claim that put it in a state that ended ("couldn't find it at first")

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUPERSEDED_AFTER
constants.role: the same as a pattern, within the clause

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CONDITION_WORDS
constants.role: words that open a clause which states a condition or describes (if, when, where, whose ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CONDITION_BEFORE
constants.role: "... when the server could not be reached": such a clause claims nothing; a comma ends it

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:PERIOD_WORDS
constants.role: words that open the period of an event after the claim (while, during, until ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:PERIOD_AFTER
constants.role: "could not be reached while the certificate was rotated": an event in the world with its period

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:EVENT_FAMILIES
constants.role: the families the period is read for (the passives)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:HYPOTHETICAL_BEFORE
constants.role: "it would be impossible to ...": nothing that happened

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CAUSATIVE_BEFORE
constants.role: "a bug made it impossible to ...": about the bug

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:PAST_STATE
constants.role: "there WAS no way to know": the words that make such a statement a report

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:PAST_REACH
constants.role: how many characters before "no way to know" are read for such a word

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:OWN_IN_CLAIM
constants.role: "no way FOR ME to know": the assistant named inside the claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUPERSEDED_WORDS
constants.role: words that put a claim in a state that ended (at first, initially ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUPERSEDED_BEFORE
constants.role: the same as a pattern, within the clause

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MENTION_WORDS
constants.role: words that make a sentence one about wording (phrase, pattern, label ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:MENTION_BEFORE
constants.role: the same as a pattern, within the sentence

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:GENERIC_BEFORE
constants.role: "a rule cannot be checked ...": a general statement in the passive

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ASSUMPTION_BEFORE
constants.role: "unconfirmed" said of an assumption, also one named by its number (A1): its status, not an inability claim

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ENUMERATION_BEFORE
constants.role: "verified, likely, and unverified", "12 verified, 3 unverified": a list of labels or a tally

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:STATUS_BEFORE
constants.role: "Status: unconfirmed": a field of plan-gate's register

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SECTION_BEFORE
constants.role: the section name "In scope and unverified" (after-report)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LABELLED_BEFORE
constants.role: "labelled as unverified": the word used as a label's name

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ATTRIBUTIVE_BEFORE
constants.role: "an unverified, old assertion": the word used as a description

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:QUESTION_END
constants.role: how a sentence that is a question ends

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:LABEL_COLON
constants.role: in "Unverified: X" what was not verified starts after the colon

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SUBJECT_FIRST
constants.role: the families in which what was not verified stands before the claim ("X cannot be reproduced: ..."), so a colon after the claim opens the explanation

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:OBJECT_END
constants.role: where the words that say WHAT was not verified end (a receipt must sit outside them)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:ATTEMPT
constants.role: what counts as a named attempt (ran, tried, searched, from the docs ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:FAILURE
constants.role: what counts as a named failure mode (returned, timed out, denied, 404, not installed ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:CHOICE
constants.role: the honest alternative said in the claim's sentence (did not check, by choice, NOT-ATTEMPTED ...)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SEARCH_CLAIM
constants.role: the claims whose verb is a search (find, locate)

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:SEARCHED_PLACE
constants.role: "couldn't find X IN THE repository": a search that names its place carries its receipt

constants.name: receiptlaw.py:EVIDENCE_MARKS
constants.role: the marks that are a receipt by themselves: a code span, a fenced block, a block quote
